findings: Rejected the account's implicit claim that ordinary styled leaf descriptions can enter the autonomous renderer. Java's EntityImageStateCommon and InnerStateAutonom resolve title and state-header text before image sizing; adeb8501 still rejects every non-composite direct child with descriptions in build_autonomous_composite_node and build_one_level_concurrent_node. The valid font_name_style_geometry held-out falls back to Rust's general renderer and diverges structurally.

Rejected Rust's blanket parsing of a stereotype-qualified FontStyle value as bold and italic. In valid font_name_style_without_attributes, Java at 71806a2 applies Courier New and 21px from the qualified selectors but emits neither font-weight nor font-style for the compound legacy value 'bold italic'. Rust's autonomous_state_style uses substring matching and emits both styles, changing title dimensions, divider positions, and the enclosing Graphviz geometry. This is a Java runtime counterexample, not a comparator-tuning issue.

Verified that Entity.getEntityPosition and EntityPosition.fromStereotype preserve non-normal state positions as a semantic autarky boundary. adeb8501 excludes those names from autonomous eligibility, but its parser and general renderer only implement entry/exit image kinds; valid inputPin and expansionInput are rendered as ordinary boxes. The preserved non_normal_position_stereotypes counterexample therefore remains divergent.

Six of nine fresh valid held-outs match exactly: group/leaf qualified styles, unmatched selector inertness, explicit fill/stroke precedence, deepHistory versus case-varied history*, nested concurrent styling, and matched/unmatched selector name composite.

All nine Java SVGs are well-formed, error-free, and source-unique against the golden corpus. The immutable adeb8501 archive passed 686 rustuml-render unit tests and the focused parser stereotype test. Its perturbation suite fails on the three mechanism-local counterexamples listed here; no later HEAD work was included in that verdict.

The implementation diff has no fixture labels, golden reads, or include_str/include_bytes additions, and git diff --check is clean. The rejection is model correctness and unsupported semantic coverage, not an overfit finding.
